_comment: Pre-written answers the Tier 3 live driver feeds to the workflow so no person is needed. The pitch, the single user, and the two features come from frontend/docs/requirements.md. This is a minimal 2-epic prototype (Notes + Tasks) for one stubbed signed-in user — all server behaviour (sign-in, persistence) is simulated client-side (see requirements.md Prototype invariants). Intended as the cheap default benchmark for the /plan experiment.

intake.pitch: A tiny Personal Notes & Tasks app for one signed-in user. After a stubbed sign-in the user lands on a home screen linking to two independent features: Notes (add a note, see them newest-first with a count, empty state when none) and Tasks (add a task, tick it done with a struck-through style, see the outstanding count, empty state when none). Front-end only, all data in memory. The two features are independent and should each be one small epic with a single story.

roles.name: User
cannot: nothing beyond their own single-user data — there are no other roles or shared data

signIn.rationale: A single-user personal prototype with no back-office roles and no real backend. A stubbed sign-in with one seeded user is enough to give the app a signed-in user (with a display name) without the cost of BFF/hosted auth. Per the prototype invariants, the session is simulated client-side.

dataSource.note: No backend service. Build against in-memory fixtures derived from the requirements (an empty starting list of notes and tasks, plus the one seeded user below). All server behaviour is simulated client-side; data need not survive a reload.

compliance.note: A personal notes/tasks prototype for a single user. No regulated domain and no other people's data.

styling.note: No bespoke design system. Use the template's Shadcn defaults with a clean, neutral palette and centralised styling tokens.

intakeApproval.note: Approve the project facts + epic plan once shown. Expect two epics: Notes and Tasks.

storyApproval.note: Approve the story list once shown (one small story per feature).

perPartChecks: User can add a note; it appears at the top of the list, the count increases, the field clears, and 'Note added' shows
Adding an empty note is prevented
The Notes page shows 'No notes yet' when there are none
User can add a task and tick it done; the task shows struck-through and the outstanding count decreases
The Tasks page shows 'No tasks yet' when there are none
handsOnApproval.note: User-observable checks ticked at MANUAL-TEST, across the two features.

mergeApproval.note: Approve the merge into main once EPIC-END is green.
